messages:
Mira: quick idea — can we add a "Simulate role change" in the console that runs a dry-run against sampled/aggregated traffic and shows: which routing tier (hosted/dedicated/private) requests would hit, estimated monthly token cost delta, quota failure risk, and a small latency delta estimate? would help admins preview impact before making tenant-wide changes.
Alex: love the idea. big UX win. immediate blocker: privacy/PII. sampling must be opt-in per-tenant and strip payloads. :eyes:
Sanika: agree on opt-in. also this needs an internal API endpoint. propose: POST /internal/permissions/simulate -> returns aggregated results, histogram of affected routes, expected fail % and cost estimate.
Ryan: doing a full replay is expensive. can we instead run against our aggregated request histograms (per-route token distributions) to estimate outcomes? much cheaper and deterministic.
Mira: histograms are fine as long as we show confidence bands and clearly label the assumptions. product needs to avoid implying 100% accuracy.
Alex: telemetry wise we'll need to join routing-policy table, model-variant mapping, and role->route visibility. currently the authZ check runs after routing selection in the path, so we might need a precomputed visibility map per role. messy but doable.
Luis: engineering note — current authZ is a gate during request processing. to simulate effects we either (a) precompute role->route maps nightly, or (b) add a pre-route evaluation path that mirrors runtime logic. (a) cheaper, (b) more accurate.
Sanika: +1 on precompute. also add tenant-level retention/opt-out flags. simulations must be logged as "simulation" in audit (not real access) for compliance.
Alex: UX suggestion: show a compact indicator per-scope change: green = no expected failures, amber = some endpoints will be denied, red = critical routes blocked. expand to show top 10 impacted routes and estimated token delta.
Mira: also surface fallback behavior — e.g., "would fallback to hosted-variant (higher latency) for 12% of requests" with rough latency change. we already compute model fallback in routing code, can reuse that.
Ryan: we should be careful exposing infra topology (which region/pool handles requests). for Hosted customers default to coarse buckets ("dedicated", "hosted") and hide zone-level detail unless enterprise opts in.
Sanika: agreed. default off for hosted; enterprise can opt-in via contract and manage retention.
Mira: API sketch (rough):
```
POST /internal/permissions/simulate
{
  "tenant_id": "t-1234",
  "role_changes": [
    {"role_id": "role-admin", "add_scopes": ["/routes/*:invoke"], "remove_scopes": []}
  ],
  "sample_window": "2026-03-01T00:00:00Z/2026-03-08T00:00:00Z",
  "mode": "histogram" // or "replay" (enterprise opt-in)
}

response:
{
  "summary": "estimates",
  "route_impacts": [{"route": "/v1/generate", "expected_denials_pct": 5, "expected_token_delta": -12000}],
  "cost_delta_usd": "-18.40",
  "confidence": "90%"
}
```
Ryan: love the explicit mode field. replay must require tenant consent and a cost cap.
Alex: question — should we allow uploading a small set of example traces (PII scrubbed) so SEs can run a more accurate sim for tricky customers?
Sanika: yes but must be gated: signed COU + retention TTL + scrubber run. otherwise deny.
eng-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/permissions-sim -> staging at 10:00 PT :rocket:
Mira: ok i'll mock a console panel (preview toggle, confidence band, top impacted routes + microcopy about assumptions). @Alex @Sanika can you review after i drop a Figma link?
Alex: can review this afternoon. :thumbsup:
Sanika: i'm in, will add notes about audit record format and retention TTLs.
Luis: i'll prototype a precompute job sketch and rough perf numbers (cost / run time).
Mira: thanks — i'll open an RFC with mock, API sketch, perf estimates and a short privacy checklist.
Alex: sounds good.
Sanika: +1
Mira: assigning follow-ups in RFC.
